task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm having trouble with my mobile data — it either stops working completely or is just really slow. I'd really like to get it working properly with excellent internet speed. I don't have access to Wi-Fi right now, so my mobile data is all I've got.

turns.thought: I'd be glad to help you get your mobile data working well. First, I need to look up your account. Could you please provide your phone number, or your full name and date of birth?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought: I've found the issue. Let me check what other plan options are available for you.

turns.thought:
I found your account, John. You have three lines:
- **555-123-2001** (L1001) – Active, Basic Plan
- **555-123-2002** (L1002) – Active, Premium Plan (this is the number you gave me)
- **555-123-2003** (L1003) – Suspended

Let me check a few things on your device. First, could you look at your status bar — what icons do you see at the top of your screen? While you do that, let me run a check.

I've found your account, John. Before I proceed, let me confirm a couple of details about your line **555-123-2002**:

- Line status: **Active** (not suspended)
- Plan: **Premium Plan** — 15.0 GB data limit
- Data used this cycle: **15.1 GB** (cycle ends 2025-02-28)

Your usage has gone over your plan's 15.0 GB limit, which is why your data has been cutting out or crawling — when the limit is exceeded, data connectivity is lost.

To get you back up and running, I can add more data to this line ("refueling"). Your plan's rate is **$2.00 per GB**, and the maximum I can add is **2 GB**.

How much data would you like me to add — 1 GB ($2.00) or 2 GB ($4.00)?

(Just to note: I wasn't able to run any device-side diagnostics, so if the problem continues after refueling, let me know and I'll dig further.)
turns.execution_output: User: Oh, I see — that makes sense then. I had no idea I'd gone over. Let's go ahead and add the full 2 GB, please. I want to make sure I have enough to get through the rest of the month.
{"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
All set — 2 GB has been added to your line **555-123-2002** for **$4.00** (at your plan's rate of $2.00/GB). This charge will be added to your account.

Your line now shows:
- Data used: 15.1 GB
- Plan limit: 15.0 GB
- Refueled data added: 2.0 GB
- Cycle ends: 2025-02-28

One caveat: I wasn't able to run a speed test on your device from here (that diagnostic isn't available to me right now), so I can't personally confirm your speed has reached "excellent." Please try your mobile data again and let me know how it performs.

Also, since this is the 2 GB maximum refuel, if you run through this before the cycle resets on 2025-02-28, the same slowdown will happen again. If that's a recurring problem, I can walk you through changing to a plan with a higher data limit.

Is there anything else I can help with?
turns.execution_output: User: Let me try it out and see how it's performing now.

turns.thought: I'm sorry it didn't resolve it — let's dig into the device settings themselves. Let me run some diagnostics.

I'm sorry this is still not working — I understand the frustration, especially with no Wi-Fi available.

Let me be straightforward with you: every device-side diagnostic and fix I'd normally use to continue troubleshooting (checking network status, APN settings, mobile data switch, roaming, signal strength, airplane mode, and running a speed test) is currently unavailable to me. Without those, I can't safely diagnose why you're still seeing "No Connection" — and I don't want to send you in circles with guesses.

What I can confirm from your account side is all clear:
- Line 555-123-2002 is **Active** (not suspended)
- The 2 GB refuel was applied successfully (15.1 GB used / 15.0 limit + 2.0 GB refueled)
- Your bill B1002 is **Issued**, not overdue

Since the remaining steps are all device-side and I can't perform or verify them, I'm going to transfer you to a human agent who has access to the full diagnostic toolset so they can get you back online.

Would that be alright with you?
turns.execution_output: User: I appreciate the honesty, but before we transfer — I'm happy to poke around in my phone's settings myself if you tell me what to look at. I can check things like my signal bars, whether mobile data is switched on, airplane mode, that kind of thing, and read back to you what I see. Would that help? I'd rather try that first than start over with someone new.

turns.thought:
Yes, absolutely — that would help a lot. Your eyes on the phone can stand in for the diagnostics I can't run. Let's start with the quickest, most informative one.

**Step 1 — Look at the status bar (very top of your screen) and read back to me:**

1. **Airplane mode**: Do you see an airplane ✈️ icon anywhere?
2. **Signal**: Do you see any signal bars at all, or does it say "No Signal"? If there are bars, roughly how many (1, 2, 3, 4)?
3. **Network type**: Next to the bars, what does it say — 5G, LTE/4G, 3G, H+, E, or 2G? Or nothing at all?
4. **Mobile data**: Is there any indication data is off or restricted (sometimes shown as an up/down arrow missing, or a "data disabled" note)?
5. **Data Saver**: Do you see a Data Saver / restricted-data icon (often looks like a downward arrow or a circle with a slash)?
6. **VPN**: Do you see a key 🔒 or VPN icon?

Take your time and just tell me whatever you can see (or don't see) for each. That'll let me narrow down whether this is a settings issue, a signal issue, or something on the line/account side.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at my status bar now.

turns.thought:
That's very helpful — and I think we've found it. **Airplane mode is ON**, and that's almost certainly the whole problem: it disconnects every wireless radio, including cellular. That perfectly explains "No Connection" and no signal bars or network type showing.

**Please turn Airplane Mode OFF.** Two quick ways:

- **Fastest:** Swipe down from the very top of your screen (on some phones, swipe down twice) to open the Quick Settings panel. Find the **Airplane mode** tile and tap it so it turns off/gray. The ✈️ icon should disappear from the status bar.
- **Through Settings:** Open **Settings → Network & internet** (or **Connections**) → toggle **Airplane mode** to OFF.

Then give it about 10–20 seconds to reconnect to the network, and run your speed test again.

Let me know:
- Did the ✈️ icon go away?
- Do you now see signal bars and a network type (5G / LTE / etc.)?
- What does the speed test report now?

One note: your VPN (🔒) is also connected. Let's deal with that *after* we see whether airplane mode fixes things — a VPN can sometimes slow data considerably, but it isn't your main issue right now, so I don't want to change two things at once and muddy the result.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me turn airplane mode off.

turns.thought:
Yes — please turn mobile data on. That "Data Disabled" indicator is the next thing blocking you.

**How to turn it on:**
- **Fastest:** Swipe down from the top of your screen to open Quick Settings, find the **Mobile data** tile (sometimes labeled "Data" or shown with up/down arrows), and tap it so it's enabled/blue.
- **Through Settings:** **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network** (or **Connections → Data usage**) → toggle **Mobile data** to ON.

Then wait a few seconds and run the speed test again.

Also, while you're in that **Mobile network** screen, look for an option called **Preferred network type** / **Network mode** and tell me what it's currently set to. You're on **2G** right now, and 2G isn't capable of anything beyond a crawl — even with data enabled, you likely won't get usable speeds on it. We may want to change that, but let's confirm the mobile data toggle first so we know what actually fixed what.

Report back:
- Does the 📵 "Data Disabled" indicator go away?
- Do you see up/down arrows or a data icon now?
- What does the speed test say?
- What's your **Preferred network type** currently set to?

Still 1 bar / "Poor" signal — we'll look at that next if speed is still bad, but let's get data switched on first.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me turn mobile data on.

turns.thought:
Yes, let's do the network mode — that's very likely the remaining blocker. **2G genuinely cannot carry a usable data connection**, and a speed test reporting "No Connection" on 2G is exactly what I'd expect even with mobile data switched on. You've made real progress: airplane mode off, data on. The network mode is the last big one.

**Please change your preferred network type:**
- Go to **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Preferred network type** (on some phones it's under **Advanced**, or labeled **Network mode**)
- It's currently on 2G — change it to **5G/4G (recommended)**, or if that's not offered, **4G/LTE** or **3G**

Make sure you don't pick a "2G only" option. Then wait 15–20 seconds for it to re-register on the network and run the speed test again.

Two more things on your list:

**Data Saver (🔽)** — please turn this off once you've checked the network mode. It restricts background data and can make things feel stalled or slow. It's usually at **Settings → Network & internet → Data Saver** → toggle off.

**VPN (🔒)** — leave it connected for now. Let's get the network mode change tested on its own first.

One thing I want to flag honestly: your signal is **1 bar / "Poor"**. Even on 5G/4G, a poor signal will limit your speed — you may not reach "excellent." Poor signal is usually about your physical location (basement, dense building, distance from a tower). Once we've got data flowing on a better network mode, we can talk about what to do about signal strength if speed is still low.

Let me know: what was your preferred network type set to, what you changed it to, and what the speed test says now.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check what my network mode is currently set to first.

turns.thought:
That's genuinely useful progress, even though the result looks the same — your phone went from 2G/1 bar to **Excellent signal on 5G**. So the radio, the network mode, and the tower connection are all working. "No Connection" with a strong 5G signal means something *on the phone* is still blocking or misrouting the data — not your coverage.

So yes, let's clear the two remaining blockers. I know it's tedious, but please change them **one at a time and retest after each**, so we know which one actually did it (and it stops us flailing if neither works).

**Step 1 — Turn Data Saver OFF**
- **Settings → Network & internet → Data Saver** → toggle **Off**
- (On some phones: **Settings → Connections → Data usage → Data Saver**)
- The 🔽 icon should disappear from your status bar.

Wait ~10 seconds, then run the speed test.

**Step 2 — If it still fails, disconnect the VPN**
- **Settings → Network & internet → VPN** → tap the gear/settings next to your VPN → **Disconnect** or toggle it off
- (Or swipe down to Quick Settings and tap the **VPN** tile — that usually disconnects it instantly)
- The 🔒 icon should go away.

Wait ~10 seconds, then run the speed test again.

Tell me after each one: did the icon disappear, and what does the speed test say?

**If neither of those fixes it**, my next suspect is your **APN settings** (specifically the MMSC/APN config your phone uses to reach the carrier's data network). That's a settings-repair I can walk you through — it involves resetting APN to default and then rebooting. It's a bit more involved, so I wanted to rule out these two first.

I do hear you on the frustration — we've fixed four things and you're still stuck. But each one we rule out narrows it meaningfully, and a strong 5G signal tells me we're close to the actual cause rather than chasing a coverage problem.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me turn Data Saver off first.

turns.thought:
Yes — your status bar is now completely clean and correct (4 bars, Excellent, 5G, data enabled, no restrictions), so the APN is the right next suspect. That's actually a good sign: your signal and settings are fine, so this is likely a config issue we can reset.

**Walking you through the APN reset:**

1. Open **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network**
2. Scroll down and tap **Access Point Names** (or **APN**) — it may be under **Advanced**
3. You'll see a list with a selected/dotted entry. **First, check what's there:** look at the **APN** value and the **MMSC** field and tell me what they say (or if MMSC is blank)
4. Tap the **⋮ menu** (three dots, top-right) → **Reset to default** — then confirm
5. Wait for the reset to confirm/repopulate the list

**Yes — you will need to reboot.** This is the part people miss: APN changes don't take effect until the phone restarts. Please:
- Hold the **power button** → **Restart** (or power off, wait 10 seconds, power back on)
- After it comes back up, wait ~20–30 seconds for it to re-register on 5G, then run the speed test

That's a genuine, known fix — misconfigured APN (especially a missing MMSC/APN entry) will produce exactly your symptom: perfect signal, everything enabled, still "No Connection."

Two notes before you start:
- Resetting APN to default won't delete anything personal — it only restores carrier network settings.
- While you're in there, if you happen to see a **Carrier** or **Network operators** option with "Select automatically" turned off, that'd be worth mentioning, but don't change it on your own.

Do the reset, reboot, and let me know what the speed test says. And on the frustration — you're right to feel it, five steps is a lot. But a clean status bar plus a pending APN reset is a genuinely promising position, not a dead end. If the APN reset and reboot don't fix it, I'll hand you to a human agent with a full record of everything we've ruled out, so you won't be starting from zero with someone new.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check my APN settings first before resetting.

turns.thought:
Good question to ask before changing it — let me think about this properly rather than just pushing ahead.

Looking at what you've got:

- **APN name: `internet`** — that's a filled-in, plausible value, but I honestly can't verify from here that it's the *correct* one for our carrier's data network. A wrong (but populated) APN produces exactly your symptom: full signal, everything enabled, dead data.
- **MMSC URL: populated** — that field matters for picture messaging (MMS), not for general internet data. So it doesn't really tell us anything about your data connection either way.

So: this doesn't definitively confirm the APN is good, and it doesn't confirm it's broken. It's populated, which is mildly reassuring, but not proof.

**My recommendation: yes, go ahead with the reset.** Here's my reasoning:
- Reset-to-default is a low-risk, reversible action — it only touches carrier network settings, nothing personal, and it restores the correct carrier defaults rather than deleting anything
- It's the last fix available to us before escalation, and it's a legitimate fix for your exact symptom
- Even if the APN turns out to be fine, the **reboot** that follows is worth doing on its own — we've changed airplane mode, network mode, data, Data Saver, and VPN on this device, and a restart clears any stuck state from all that churn. There's a real chance the reboot alone helps.

**Sequence:**
1. **⋮ menu → Reset to default** → confirm
2. **Reboot** (hold power → Restart)
3. Wait ~20–30 seconds after restart for 5G to re-register
4. Run the speed test

If it works — great, we're done. If it *doesn't*, I'll transfer you to a human agent, and I'll pass along the complete picture: your account and line are active and healthy, the 2 GB refuel (for $4.00) was applied successfully, and we've ruled out airplane mode, data disabled, 2G network mode, Data Saver, VPN, and now APN — on a clean 5G/Excellent signal. You won't be repeating any of this with them.

Go ahead and let me know how it goes.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me reset the APN to default.
